paras: Deep in a forest lived a lion named Bhasuraka, so proud and cruel that he killed animals not only for food but for fun. The frightened animals held a meeting and went to him together. “Your Majesty,” they said, “if you keep hunting like this, the forest will soon be empty. Stay in your den instead, and every day one of us will come to you as your meal.” The lion agreed, but warned that if a single day was missed, he would kill them all.

Day after day, an animal went to the lion. Then came the turn of a small rabbit. The rabbit was afraid, but he was also clever. On the way he walked slowly, stopping to think, and by the time he reached the den the sun was high and the lion was roaring with hunger.
“Why are you so late?” thundered the lion. “And you are so small! You would not fill even one of my teeth!”

The rabbit bowed low. “Your Majesty, it is not my fault. Five rabbits were sent to you today. But on the way, another lion stopped us. He said that he is the true king of this forest, and he ate the other four. I alone escaped to bring you the news.”
The lion's eyes blazed. “Another king in my forest? Show me this thief at once!”
The rabbit led him to an old, deep well. “He lives down there, Your Majesty, inside his fortress.”

The lion peered into the well and saw a fierce lion glaring up at him from the water. It was his own reflection. He roared, and the well roared back even louder. Mad with fury, the lion leapt into the well to fight his rival, and was never seen again.
The rabbit ran back to the other animals with the news, and the whole forest rejoiced.
Moral: Intelligence is greater than strength.
